turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels,
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and the two measured objectives `yield
    strength (MPa)` and `toughness (J)` (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose
    objectives were NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH toughness (J). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), toughness (J)) plane, so a set of mutually
non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates that are
all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Where the frontier lies.** In the 300 training steels the (YS, toughness) Pareto front runs roughly:

| YS (MPa) | Toughness (J) | Alloy/treatment family |
|---|---|---|
| 270–380 | 300–370 | solution-annealed high-Cr-Ni austenitics (23Cr-18/27Ni, Mo, Cu) |
| 710–730 | 210–230 | Cr-Mo-V medium-C steel with intercritical + 650–680 °C temper; solution-annealed maraging |
| 900–1000 | 100–130 | Ti-strengthened A286-type (11Cr-19/23Ni-2.9Ti) with double age; low-C 5Cr |
| 1300–1580 | 20–75 | 11–13 Cr martensitics tempered 300–500 °C; Cu/Ti PH-martensitic (12.5Cr-8.5Ni-1.75Cu) aged 400–450 °C |

So the frontier is dominated by *alloy class + tempering/aging temperature*: austenitic & solution-annealed = tough/soft; martensitic with low-temperature temper = strong/brittle; A286-type and intercritically tempered Cr-Mo-V occupy the useful middle.

**2. Mapping pool candidates onto near-identical training rows**

- **c010** (23.5Cr-27Ni-2.75Mo-3Cu, 1050 °C/4.6 h WQ, no aging) ≈ the 270 MPa / **350 J** training record (highest toughness in the set) → toughness anchor.
- **c085** (2.35Cr-1Mo-0.4V-0.26C, 1040 °C → 960 °C → 675 °C/6 h) ≈ training row with 960 °C+680 °C giving **710 MPa / 230 J**; the 650 °C variant gave 780/120 → excellent mid-frontier point (~730 / ~210).
- **c060** (11.25Cr-23Ni-2.9Ti-1.3Mo, solution + 845 °C + 710 °C double age) ≈ the A286-type row that gave **1000 MPa / 100 J** (same base alloy, double age) → high-strength/moderate-toughness middle.
- **c041** (11.25Cr-1.65Ni-V-W-0.13C, 1000 °C/120, temper 450 °C) — same alloy tempered at 300 °C→1330/60, 400 °C→1340/61, 550 °C→1090/88 ⇒ ~1250 MPa with ~65–70 J.
- **c004** (12.5Cr-8.5Ni-0.75Mo-0.95Ti-1.75Cu, 880 °C/WQ + 250 °C age) — this family peaks hard: 450 °C→1578/27, 400 °C→1287/38, 550 °C→1184/100, 650 °C→800/168. An under-aged/low-temperature condition of this PH-martensitic alloy is the pool's best shot at the extreme-strength corner (and if it under-ages it still lands high-strength with better toughness).

Candidates that looked attractive but are dominated were dropped: c002/c038 (austenitics, ~240–250 MPa but only 200–230 J → dominated by c010), c072 (475 °C temper ≈ c041 but weaker), c063/c019/c027 (13Cr-0.4C, ~900–960 MPa with only ~20 J), c050/c069 (~700 MPa/35 J).

**3. Resulting spanned set** (estimated): (275, 340) – (730, 210) – (960, 100) – (1250, 65) – (≥1200, 30–90): five mutually non-dominated points spread evenly along the strength axis, which maximizes dominated hypervolume rather than clustering on one objective.

Final: c010, c085, c060, c041, c004
